title: InstaAnki real medical image assets
usage: Unmodified, licensed real images for the final clinical-example section of lessons. Keep attribution accessible in the app and in exported lesson packs.

assets.title: Coronary angiograms showing right and left dominance
assets.author: I. Kruzhilov; E. Ikryannikov; A. Shadrin; R. Utegenov; G. Zubkova; I. Bessonov
assets.sourceTitle: Neural Network-Based Coronary Dominance Classification of RCA Angiograms
assets.attribution: Kruzhilov et al., Figure 1, Doklady Mathematics 110 (Suppl 1), S212-S222 (2024; online 2025), doi:10.1134/S1064562424602026. CC BY 4.0. Unmodified.
assets.modifications: None; original published figure downloaded without alteration.
assets.caption: Real coronary angiograms: panel (a) shows a right-sided origin of the posterior descending artery; panel (b) illustrates left coronary dominance. Red arrows identify the posterior descending artery in the published figure.
assets.displayNotes: For the left-dominance lesson, direct attention to panel (b), the right half of the figure. Keep source panel labels and attribution visible or accessible. This figure illustrates dominance, not the particular occlusion described in the source MCQ.
assets.licenseEvidence: Article Rights and permissions states CC BY 4.0 and includes images unless separately credited. No separate restriction or third-party credit appears for Figure 1.
assets.clinicalEvidence: The article identifies coronary dominance by the origin of the PDA and describes the left-dominant PDA as arising from the left circumflex artery.

assets.title: Extralobar pulmonary sequestration at thoracoscopy
assets.author: Carolyn Hanna; Priya G. Sharma; Moiz M. Mustafa; Jennifer Reppucci; Archana Shenoy; Dhanashree Rajderkar
assets.sourceTitle: Concurrent bronchopulmonary foregut malformations: a rare case of right-sided extralobar pulmonary sequestration and bronchogenic cyst
assets.attribution: Hanna et al., Figure 4, Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine 52:54 (2021), doi:10.1186/s43055-021-00440-1. CC BY 4.0. Unmodified.
assets.modifications: None; original published figure downloaded without alteration.
assets.caption: Real thoracoscopic views of an extralobar pulmonary sequestration. Panel A shows the separate lesion covered by its own pleura. Panel D depicts an associated bronchogenic cyst, not the sequestration.
assets.displayNotes: Focus the lesson on panel A. Panels B and C show the stalk; panel D shows a different associated lesion. Do not highlight all four panels as if each represents the tested pleural feature.

focusRegion.label: Panel A: sequestration with its own pleural covering

assets.licenseEvidence: Article and figure page state CC BY 4.0, with images included unless separately credited. Figure 4 has no separately restrictive credit.
assets.clinicalEvidence: Figure 4 description and the case pathology identify an extralobar sequestration invested in its own pleura.

assets.title: Human artery in cross section
assets.author: Lord of Konrad; Commons color adjustment by Tilifa Ocaufa
assets.attribution: Human artery photomicrograph by Lord of Konrad; Commons color adjustment by Tilifa Ocaufa. Wikimedia Commons, Artery.png. CC0 1.0.
assets.modifications: No changes by InstaAnki. The Commons version downloaded records a 2015 color adjustment.
assets.caption: A real bright-field micrograph of a human artery. The central lumen provides anatomical context for the lesson on vessel radius and resistance.
assets.displayNotes: This is a real anatomical example, not a measurement of the numerical scenario. Do not claim that the image demonstrates a doubled diameter or a measured sixteenfold resistance change. The calculation applies to the lesson's stated idealized assumptions.
assets.licenseEvidence: The file-specific Licensing section explicitly dedicates the image to CC0 1.0; this is separate from the Commons website footer.
assets.clinicalEvidence: The creator identifies the image as a bright-field photomicrograph of a cross section of a human artery.
